title: Streaming schema enforcer + toolcall framing and tokenizer splitter for OpenAI compat
author: Emilia Chen
description:
Motivation: Streaming structured output with function/tool-calling is brittle when tokens for bracket characters or regex anchors are split across streaming chunks. This causes downstream parsers (OpenAI-compat tool callers and schema validators) to mis-parse partial frames, resulting in spurious tool invocations or broken structured outputs.

Summary: Introduce a streaming schema enforcer shim that sits in the OpenAI-compat layer and does three things: 1) atomize and reassemble tokenizer edges that would split structural tokens (quotes, braces, function-call separators) across chunks; 2) wire a lightweight CFG-aware fast-fallback parser compiled for CPU when GPU kernel path can't satisfy complex regex/grammar constraints; 3) add explicit toolcall framing markers and heuristics so partially-emitted tool payloads don't trigger tool invocation until a syntactic commit point is reached.

Key changes (single-line checklist): [x] Enforcer shim added to integrations/openai/compat_layer.py and runtime/streaming_shim.rs; [x] Tokenizer splitter/atomizer added in runtime/tokenizer/splitter.cu + fallback C implementation; [x] CFG CPU fallback engine implemented in runtime/grammar/fallback_cpu.c (small footprint + permissive fallbacks); [x] Toolcall framing rules added and exposed via API flag `prefer_strict_toolcall_framing`; [x] Unit and e2e tests (including flaky-token-chunking matrix) added under tests/e2e/; [x] Docs updated with migration notes and opt-in flags.

Design notes: The shim intercepts streaming token batches before they are forwarded to the OpenAI-compat streaming interface. It examines the tokenizer tokenization boundaries and holds back emission of structural tokens when they are part of a longer multi-token delimiter (e.g., CRLF-anchored regexes, multi-byte quote characters). When the runtime cannot guarantee atomicity on the GPU path (e.g., due to current kernel fusion heuristics), the shim falls back to a compact CFG checker on CPU to validate that the partial output cannot form a valid constraint-satisfying completion. Toolcalls are only relayed to the tool-runner once the framing heuristic sees either the full function signature and a closing marker or a validated CFG parse. This reduces false positives during streaming and ensures behavior matches batch decode semantics.

Performance: Microbenchmarks show median end-to-end streaming latency increase of ~3ms on 2048-seq workloads when shim is enabled (GPU path), with a tail P99 increase of ~12ms in the worst-case when CFG fallback is used. Unit token throughput remains within 95% of baseline in typical workloads. See perf numbers in the PR body.

Testing: Added deterministic unit tests for tokenizer atomization, property tests for chunk boundary permutations, and e2e tests exercising toolcall sequences with artificially split tokens. CI includes a new flaky-token-chunking matrix job that runs smaller variants of the chunk-split permutations to catch regressions. Locally validated against existing OpenAI-compat integration tests.

Migration and rollout: Default for `prefer_strict_toolcall_framing` is OFF; to avoid changing existing customers' runtime semantics we ship this as opt-in. For Hosted we will enable the shim behind a feature flag and roll to canary tenants first. Dedicated and Private customers can opt into the flag in their config.

Risks: The primary risk is subtle differences in toolcall timing for apps that intentionally rely on partial toolcall streaming. To mitigate we keep the flag off by default and document behavior. CFG fallback correctness for complex grammars is intentionally permissive (we prefer false negatives over false positives) and is covered by unit tests.

Related: Linear: ENG-2109 (streaming stability), ENG-2140 (tokenizer atomizer). Support ticket SUP-914 captured an incident that inspired this work.

Notes for reviewers: Look at runtime/streaming_shim.rs for the emission state machine, runtime/tokenizer/splitter.cu and splitter_fallback.c for atomization logic, and integrations/openai/compat_layer.py for wiring into function/tool-call paths. The e2e tests are the best reproducible signal (tests/e2e/toolcall_streaming.test).

review_conversation: Ravi Patel (2025-11-05): Nice direction. Two comments: 1) We need numbers on P99 impact in high concurrency, 2) please add a test where the closing brace is split across two chunks. Can you add perf counters for shim hot-path?
Emilia Chen (2025-11-06): Added e2e test covering split closing brace case and added counters (shim_emit_count, shim_fallback_count, shim_hold_ms). Updated PR with perf microbench numbers.

Diego Morales (2025-11-07): Requested change: the CFG fallback currently treats some regex anchors as strict; prefer a permissive-mode toggle. Also flagged a memory allocation on hot-path in streaming_shim.rs.
Emilia Chen (2025-11-08): Implemented permissive-mode toggle and addressed allocation by reusing a small ring buffer. Updated tests to cover permissive and strict modes.
Ava Thompson (2025-11-10): CI showed a flaky matrix failure (intermittent ordering in e2e). Re-ordered assertions and added retry-with-backoff for timing-sensitive checks. Approving pending green CI.
Sophie Li (2025-11-11): Approved — verified docs and migration notes. No security concerns after review.
release_notes: Adds an opt-in streaming schema enforcer that reduces false-positive tool invocations and improves structured-output stability across chunked token streams. Includes tokenizer atomizer/fallback and a permissive CFG CPU fallback. Opt-in via `prefer_strict_toolcall_framing`. Default OFF.

perf: minimal tail latency impact; added perf counters
